full_judgment: Futile attempt had been generated from side of condemned-prisoner during trial by way of suggestion that no marriage had been solemnised between condemned prisoner and victim of crime Alesa Begum. That attempt had been flung to the wind by Bishesh Adalat, of course, very correctly. Thanks to learned Counsel appearing for condemned prisoner that the above attempt was not regenerated before this Court at the time of hearing of Death Reference. From prosecution witnesses, specially from PW 10 Zinnat Ali who is no other than the maternal grand-father of condemned-prisoner, it had been well established that Alesa Begum was the wife of condemned-prisoner. It also came to light from the testimony of PW 14 Investigating Officer, Md Altaf Hossain that victim Alesa Begum was wife of condemned-prisoner when he brought forth evidence that accused (condemned-prisoner) identified victim Alesa Begum to be his wife. Victim Alesa Begum was found dead in the but of PW 10 Zinnat Ali where condemned-prisoner along with victim of crime stayed. In case of death of wife while she is in custody of her husband a heavy burden lies upon the husband to account for the death of the wife and husband has to explain as to how his wife met with her death and the explanation must be plausible. When the wife is killed in the house of the husband the presumption is that it is the husband who is responsible for her death. Support for this proposition is sought to be drawn from Gourangh Kumar Saha vs State, 2 BLC (AD) 126, Abdul Matleb Howlader vs State, 6 BLC AD 1, State vs Kalu Bepari, 43 DLR 249, Shamsuddin vs State 45 DLR 587 and two unreported cases State vs Md Dulal Mia and State vs Md Kaloo (wherein one of us, AK Badrul Huq J. is the author Judge)
